title.narrative: EA Romania Refugees from Ukraine – Programs 2023

description.narrative:
Contribution to Caritas Appeal: EA29/2022 Romania
Context: There are an estimated 90,000 Ukrainian refugees currently in Romania. With no end to the fighting in sight and the Russian Federation increasingly targeting civilian and energy infrastructure, many refugees face the prospect of prolonged displacement and the challenge of developing sustainable strategies to meet their basic needs. Most refugees from Ukraine struggle to meet their basic needs and access the services (especially in the areas of health and education) to which they are entitled on the basis of receiving temporary protection status.
Programme Overview: Caritas Romania and its partners will continue to support refugees from Ukraine across locations in the northern part of Romania and in the capital of Bucharest to meet medium-term needs. Locations have been selected according to needs (number of refugees staying in the area) and capacities of diocesan Caritas organizations and local partners. Diocesan Caritas organizations will continue to run Social Service Centres in at least six cities: Oradea, Sighetu Marma?iei, Baia Mare, Cluj-Napoca, Ia?i, Bucharest.
Key activities include: Objective 1: Social counselling, legal counselling, psychological support, job facilitation, and health service provision Objective 2: Access to formal and informal education in educational centres Objective 3: Access to medium term accommodation Objective 4: Provision of basic needs support through food, NFI, and medicie
